summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18.6% YoY to INR175.5 crore; FY27 guidance deferred to Q1 FY27 results.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a sequential recovery, with consolidated revenue up 18.6% YoY and 25.7% QoQ to INR175.5 crore and EBITDA up 12.9% YoY to INR16.9 crore. Capacity utilisation improved to about 78%. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR567 crore, with growth held back by SOP deferrals and model-specific weakness. Profitability was hit by mark-to-market losses on investments and a one-time INR3.6 crore employee benefit charge from Labour Code implementation. The company also announced the JV stake divestment, a tooling hive-off and a battery merger, and said FY27 guidance will come with Q1 FY27 results.

segments.name: Automotive parts
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor. Secured about INR840 crore of new business across EV and ICE in FY26, with OEM customers including Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, M&M and Honda. Around 78% of revenue comes from vehicles on the market for under 5 years.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Grew 36% in FY26 via 147 distributors and 1,264 SKUs across spare parts, service parts and accessories (including perfumes and car care). Management cites a 25%+ CAGR over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Tooling (Meraki)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 12.1% in FY26 and utilisation exceeded 90%. Developed 148 molds in FY26 and targets about 300 molds a year in three years. Q4 tooling sales were lower after a high prior-year base, with some orders deferred to Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Industrial products
segments.commentary: Grew 38% in FY26 on non-automotive applications and exports, using plastic and rubber extrusion and injection moulding.

segments.name: Battery (Avinya)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue rose 1.28x YoY and Q4 losses narrowed by about 60-70%. Management expects the segment to be profitable at standalone PBT level in FY27, with full plant utilisation targeted. Some battery orders slipped to Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 guidance given; it will be issued with Q1 FY27 results once market clarity improves.
Utilisation expected at about 78% for FY26 overall, with Q1 FY27 lower; management targets 80-82% over the next year.
Management expects FY27 margins to improve versus past years, citing utilisation, solar power in place of grid power and employee-related reforms.
Battery segment expected to be profitable at standalone PBT level in FY27 and to reach full plant utilisation.
Capex to be funded from internal accruals; gross and net debt to be held around current levels through FY27.
Management expects raw material cost inflation to be about 50% passed through to customers so far, with the remaining 50% still under discussion.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 78% in Q4 FY26; management targets 80-82% over the next year.
Tooling: 148 molds made in FY26; plan to roughly double capacity over three years to about 300 molds a year.
Battery: management expects the full plant and machinery to be used in FY27 based on existing contracts.
Capex to be funded from internal accruals; JV divestment proceeds retained on balance sheet for strategic use.

Restructuring: tooling business to move into wholly-owned subsidiary Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited, targeted by Q2 FY27 subject to approvals; Avinya Batteries merger into PPAP targeted by Q4 FY27 subject to approvals.
demand_pricing: Demand: the slowdown was tied to specific models and customers whose SOPs were delayed. Those models have now started production, and new model start-ups are expected through FY27.
Customers: VinFast and Euler Motors were added in FY26, and Kia and Mahindra business is due to start production in FY27.
Content per vehicle: about INR2,500-3,500 on average, up to INR8,000-10,000 on the high side and about INR1,000 on the low side.
Segment mix: management says about 90% of new FY27 models are SUVs, with sedan weakness the main industry issue.
Input costs: raw material prices rose sharply due to the West Asia conflict; about 50% of the increase is already passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: How is PPAP handling raw material inflation from the West Asia conflict, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Supplier price increases are being passed through to keep customer lines running. About 50% is already covered by the pass-on policy, and the remaining 50% will be discussed once the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: How will the JV stake sale proceeds be used, and will debt be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is INR103 crore and gross debt about INR195 crore. The company will keep debt around these levels for FY27 and hold the funds for strategic needs, with capex funded from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tooling sales decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tooling sales are tied to SOPs. Q4 FY25 had a high base from SOPs, and a large Maruti model drove Q4 FY26. Management expects significant tooling sales in FY27 given the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will the battery business break even, and what is the Q4 loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 battery loss was about INR40 lakh against INR1.2 crore a year earlier. The segment is expected to be profitable at standalone PBT level in FY27, with full utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 margin and utilisation expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is expected at 80-82% over the next year against about 78% in Q4. Margin gains are expected from utilisation, solar power and employee reforms. Standalone EBITDA margin excluding the wage code impact was 13% in Q4 versus 11% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What new programs, customers and content per vehicle exist?
qa_highlights.answer: VinFast and Euler were added in FY26 and Kia and Mahindra programs start in FY27. Content per vehicle averages INR2,500-3,500, with a range of INR1,000 to INR10,000.

risks_watch: FY27 guidance deferred to Q1 FY27; no outlook number provided yet.
Raw material cost pass-through: about 50% of the increase is still unrecovered from customers.
Q1 FY27 utilisation expected to be lower than Q4; deferred tooling and battery orders are expected to land in Q1.
Pending approvals for the tooling hive-off (Q2 FY27) and battery merger (Q4 FY27).
Mark-to-market losses on investments and Labour Code-related employee costs affected PAT and may recur.
Industry sedan weakness and West Asia logistics disruption.
summary.management_tone: Confident on recovery and strategic reforms, but cautious on near-term demand. Management repeatedly cited a fluid external environment and withheld FY27 guidance. Some answers on the battery and margin outlook were forward-looking and lacked hard numbers.
key_quotes: Quarter 4 financial year '26 marks a significant turning point for the company, reflecting the positive outcome of the sustained efforts and strategic initiatives undertaken over the past several quarters.

Given the evolving demanding environment and continued uncertainty, the company has decided that it will provide its financial year '27 guidance during the quarter 1 financial year '27 earnings announcement once we have a better clarity on how the market conditions are faring out.
So this year, on a stand -alone basis, this battery segment should be profitable at the PBT level.
